title: Newmark Arranges Recapitalization, Financing of Fritz Farm Lifestyle Center in Lexington, Kentucky

body_markdown:
**October 26, 2026 at 9:00 AM**


Newmark announces the Company has arranged the recapitalization of Fritz Farm, a 330,077-square-foot lifestyle center and mixed-use destination in Lexington, Kentucky. The transaction adds Kimco Realty as a preferred equity investor in the property, which Hendricks Commercial Properties (“HCP”) acquired in 2025.


Newmark President and Head of[Retail Capital Markets](https://www.nmrk.com/services/investor-solutions/capital-markets/retail-capital-markets) for North America[Conor Lalor](https://www.nmrk.com/people/conor-lalor) represented Hendricks Commercial in the transaction, while Vice Chairman[Chris Kramer](https://www.nmrk.com/people/christopher-kramer) and Associate Director[Dan Axelson](https://www.nmrk.com/people/dan-axelson) arranged $104 million in senior financing provided by funds managed by Blackstone.


“Fritz Farm is Lexington’s premier mixed-use project, drawing customers from throughout Kentucky,” said Lalor. “The partnership between Hendricks Commercial and Kimco Realty is a win-win, not only for the partners, but also for the community of Lexington that will benefit from excellent long-term stewardship of its flagship retail destination.”


Located at the intersection of Nicholasville Road and Man O’ War Boulevard, Fritz Farm is Lexington’s premier lifestyle center and home to the market’s only Whole Foods Market. The property features a curated mix of national retailers, restaurants and experiential offerings, including Apple, Sephora, Nike, lululemon, Kendra Scott, William Sonoma and other leading brands. The center is currently 92.6% occupied.


Delivered in 2017 on approximately 36 acres, Fritz Farm benefits from strong tenant sales, a diverse merchandising mix and embedded growth opportunities. The property also includes approximately six acres available for future development and development rights for additional retail and residential components.


Lexington’s economy is supported by multiple demand drivers, including the University of Kentucky, the region’s renowned equine industry and Kentucky’s bourbon sector. Fritz Farm has established itself as the state’s most-visited lifestyle center and serves as a key retail destination for both residents and visitors.
